text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.46% today, adding to a sharp 21% gain over the past two weeks. The move fits a broader rally in refining stocks driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran's attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and container ships in the Strait of Hormuz have rattled oil markets and pushed crude prices higher (U.S. oil at $96/barrel, global crude at $125), while refineries are running at 92.7% capacity. Higher oil prices and constrained global supply typically lift refiner margins, though this also depends on fuel demand and inventory levels.

The tight diesel supply outlook through 2027—driven by Iran-related disruptions, falling inventories, and strong demand—is particularly relevant to a refiner's bottom line, since diesel commands premium margins in squeezed markets. Combined with refineries already running near full capacity, the company stands to benefit from sustained pricing pressure on refined products even as crude costs rise.
